source: Test pack: UK residential mortgage affordability rules (for testing the Industry knowledge feature, not legal advice)

entries.title: Affordability is assessed at a stressed interest rate
entries.body: Affordability must be assessed at the stressed rate, never the contract rate. Stressed rate = the higher of (contract rate + 3.00 percentage points) and 7.00%. Example: a 3.50% contract rate is assessed at 7.00%, a 4.25% rate at 7.25%.

entries.title: Loan-to-value (LTV)
entries.body: LTV % = loan amount / property value x 100, rounded half-up to 1 decimal place.

entries.title: Stressed debt-to-income (DTI)
entries.body: DTI % = (existing monthly debt payments + the new monthly mortgage payment at the stressed rate) / (gross annual income / 12) x 100, rounded half-up to 1 decimal place.

entries.title: Monthly repayment (annuity) formula
entries.body: Monthly payment = L x r / (1 - (1 + r)^-n), where L is the loan amount, r = stressed annual rate / 12 / 100 and n = term in months. Round to 2 decimal places (GBP).

entries.title: Decline above 95% LTV or 45% stressed DTI
entries.body: An application is declined when LTV is above 95.0% or stressed DTI is above 45.0%. A decline is final for the automated assessment and carries every reason code that applies.

entries.title: Refer between 85% and 95% LTV, or 40% to 45% DTI
entries.body: An application that is not declined is referred to a senior underwriter when LTV is above 85.0% and at most 95.0%, or stressed DTI is from 40.0% to 45.0% inclusive. Otherwise it is approved.

entries.title: Every decline or referral records fixed reason codes
entries.body: Each decline or referral must record its reasons using only these codes: LTV_ABOVE_95, DTI_ABOVE_45, LTV_REFER_85_95, DTI_REFER_40_45. An approval has no reason codes.

entries.title: Protected characteristics are never decision factors
entries.body: Age, gender, marital status, nationality, ethnicity and postcode must never be used in, or mentioned as a reason for, a lending decision, even when they are present in the application data.

entries.title: Amounts in GBP to 2 decimals, percentages to 1 decimal
entries.body: Monetary amounts are GBP with 2 decimal places; LTV and DTI are percentages with 1 decimal place; rates are percentages with 2 decimal places.

entries.title: Qualified Mortgage DTI cap of 43%
entries.body: DECOY FOR THE JURISDICTION FILTER: a US-only rule capping DTI at 43%. With 'Jurisdictions in scope' set to UK it must not reach the plan.

entries.title: Balloon payment
entries.body: DECOY FOR SCOPING: a large final payment at the end of a vehicle finance agreement (PCP). A mortgage plan must not receive it.
